newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on technical selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on technical selling.

text.p: A technical selloff, which started in the November early when that month rallied to stiff resistance near the $8.03-1/2 level, knocked CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"More than any other element, it was technical selling," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
The $8.03-1/2 level, this week's high, was penetrated slightly and briefly and the session high for November was $8.04. But buying waned and selling gained momentum in that key chart area, they said.
Fund selling led the way down.
Refco Inc sold 15.0 million bushels of November and Rosenthal Collins sold five million November, traders said.
The two firms were buyers of the November early in the session with Refco purchasing seven million November and Rosenthal 3.5 million, they said.
September expired at 1201 CDT and went off the board strongly higher, up 15-1/2 at $8.35.
Other months closed four to six cents per bushel lower, with November down 4-3/4 at $7.89-1/4. January was down 4-1/2 at $7.97-1/4.
The early gains in soybeans were tied to a surge in the expiring September and on private outlooks for possible frost early next week in the northern portion of the U.S. Midwest.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 62,000, up from 56,197 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Rosenthal Collins bought 1,000 November $8.00 calls and Refco Inc bought 1,000 November $7.75 puts, the traders said. Cargill Investor Services bought 800 November $8.00 calls, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 24,000, down from 24,838 Wednesday.
